limitations: One finite OFF/ON pair at each tested nominal power setting is not sustained operation, speech qualification, a stock-APD comparison or an all-band claim.
Absolute power and ADC clipping/headroom remain uncalibrated; LP-100A integration is deferred. Reported watts are radio samples, not independently calibrated power.
Natural 128-sample alignment slip and historical cold-start all-bypass root causes remain open. Successful acquisitions do not resolve those failures.
Cold correction acquisition remains close to the eight-second source boundary; no source limit or unkey guard was extended.

Each broker teardown reported one output error and loss_seen=1 after its stopped session; DSP end-of-run fault counters and input limiting were zero. This does not prove loss-free scheduling for arbitrary durations.
Stop retains an unprivileged private control peer/supervisor for stopped status. IQ/DSP workers, packet descriptors and temporary ARP are removed; it is not a single-process baseline.
One commanded reboot proves this release restarts and retains identity on this 8600; physical power loss, interrupted transactions and actual FLEX-6300 remain separate gates.
Development publisher pins only; production catalogue, independent review, cross-platform and release gates remain. Full P1-P10 objective is unchanged.
harness_notes: Upgrade driver matched terminal text without the cleanup suffix; its read-only polling was interrupted only after actual full GUI confirmation. One approval, no retry.
Initial post-reboot receive script toggled an already-open DAX panel closed; bridge refused the hidden selector. Reopened it and completed receive-only validation before RF.
Initial audit invocation had an invalid local hash argument and was rejected before radio activity; the actual audit used the exact diagnostic package hash.
